My family has farmed this land for generations. I have about 10 mu — same as always. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer corn on the same fields, one after the other. That's what my father did, that's what my neighbors do, and that's what works. I'm not going to try anything new at my age.

For the wheat, I'll plant in October after the autumn rain. I'll use the improved seeds from the county seed station — not the old varieties, those yields are too low. I'll apply urea and compound fertilizer like I always do. Three or four waterings: before winter sets in, again at jointing, then heading. Maybe one more if it's dry at grain fill. I'll spray herbicide in spring and fungicide once I see any rust or powdery mildew signs.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant corn immediately. I'll use hybrid seed — no question on that, yields are much better. Corn gets summer rain so I only irrigate once or twice if there's a drought. I'll put down fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea when it's about knee-high. One pesticide spray for stem borer if needed.

I use rotary tillage for wheat bed prep. For corn I direct-seed into the wheat stubble — saves time and keeps the soil from drying out too fast.
